record.original_question: Do there exist two irreducible algebraic curves of degrees n and m with n+m>4, each containing an oval, such that the associated Poncelet map is well defined and conjugate to a rotation of the circle?

evidence.quote: Problem 23. Are there two irreducible algebraic curves of degrees n and m, with n+m > 4, having each one of them an oval, for which the Poncelet's map P is well defined and it is conjugated to a rotation of the circle?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C_1, C_2 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be two irreducible real algebraic curves of degrees $n$ and $m$ respectively, with $n+m > 4$, and assume that each of $C_1$ and $C_2$ contains an oval (a smooth, connected, bounded, simple closed component of its real locus). Define the Poncelet map $P$ associated with the pair $(C_1, C_2)$ as follows: given a point $x$ on the oval of $C_1$, draw a tangent line $\ell$ to the oval of $C_2$ through $x$; the line $\ell$ meets the oval of $C_1$ in (generically) one other point $x'$, and one sets $P(x) = x'$. Assume the construction can be made consistent so that $P$ is a well-defined homeomorphism of the oval of $C_1$ to itself (homeomorphic to a circle $S^1$).

Question: Do there exist such curves $C_1, C_2$ (with $n+m>4$) for which the Poncelet map $P$ is well defined and is topologically conjugate to a rotation of the circle?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of this generalized Poncelet question for pairs of irreducible algebraic curves of degrees $n,m$ with $n+m>4$ each carrying an oval. The classical Poncelet closure theorem covers the conic case ($n=m=2$); extensions to higher-degree curves remain a topic of active investigation, but no source was found that confirms or refutes the existence of such a pair conjugating the Poncelet map to a rotation. Status is therefore taken as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Poncelet theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Classical Poncelet closure theorem and generalizations are discussed for conics; higher-degree extensions are not resolved here.
status_evidence.claim: Classical Poncelet results cover conics; the higher-degree extension is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Poncelet triangles: conic loci ...
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on Poncelet families remains focused on conics rather than higher-degree irreducible curves with ovals.
status_evidence.claim: Current literature on Poncelet maps continues to focus on the conic case.
